#  11220 - Future Technologies in Power Plants Modulübersicht  
|  Module Number:   | **11220 - module is no longer offered from SS 2017**  |  
| --- | --- |  
| Module Title:  | **Future Technologies in Power Plants**  |  
|  Zukunftstechnologien in Kraftwerken   |  
| Department:  |  Faculty 3 - Mechanical Engineering, Electrical and Energy Systems   |  
| Responsible Staff Member:  | 
  * Prof. Dr.-Ing. Krautz, Hans-Joachim 

 |  
| Language of Teaching / Examination:  | English  |  
| Duration:  | 1 semester  |  
| Frequency of Offer:  |  Every summer semester   |  
| Credits:  |  
| Learning Outcome:  | Students will acquire knowledge about emerging technologies in power generation. They will be able to identify the need and trend of future power plant technologies in relation to the environmental issues and economic aspect  |  
| Contents:  | Supercritical and Ultra-supercritical steam power plants; Boiler and Steam turbine Materials for high pressure and temperature applications; Integrated Gasification Combined Cycle (IGCC); Indirect fired combined cycle; Magnetohydrodynamics (MHD); Emerging Coal Combustion technologies (pressurized fluidized bed combustion, oxy fuel combustion and chemical looping combustion); Advanced gas turbine and gas-steam combined cycles; Solar-steam turbine hybrid power plants; solar-gas turbine hybrid power plants ; Energy storage (Battery, Compressed air)  |  
| Recommended Prerequisites:  | Basic of Thermodynamics, Energy resources and conversion, Heat transfer, Fluid mechanics  |  
| Mandatory Prerequisites:  | Module 35449 Power plant Technology I  |  
| Forms of Teaching and Proportion:  | 
  * Seminar / 4 Hours per Week per Semester 
  * Self organised studies / 120 Hours 

 |  
| Teaching Materials and Literature:  | Script  |  
| Module Examination:  | Continuous Assessment (MCA)  |  
| Assessment Mode for Module Examination:  | 
  * Homework: Written report on a given topic ( 
  * Presentation and discussion of the topic in class (45 minutes)

The final mark is based on the report (75%) and the presentation (25%).  |  
| Evaluation of Module Examination:  | Performance Verification – graded  |  
| Limited Number of Participants:  | None  |  
| Part of the Study Programme:  | 
  * no assignment

 |  
| Remarks:  | The contents of the course are not limited to the topics listed above. Based on the developments of new technologies, additional topics can be added whenever deemed necessary  |  
| Module Components:  | Future Technologies in Power Plants  |  
| Components to be offered in the Current Semester:  | 
  * no assignment

 |
